newsitem.title: USA: Centerior $700 mln debt deal tops US corps.
newsitem.headline: Centerior $700 mln debt deal tops US corps.

text.p: Centerior Energy's $700 million refinancing of its secured lease obligation bonds of its Mansfield generating plant should grab the same strong demand as most other new issues this week, dealers said.

Centerior, on review for upgrade by Moody's Investors Service following its September 16 announcement to merge with Ohio Edison Co, will issue first mortgage bonds on Wednesday to replace outstanding secured lease obligation bonds.
While helping Centerior's balance sheet, the refinancing will also water down assets backing outstanding debt, creating some question as to bondholder protections, analysts said.

"You're adding another $700 million in first mortgage bonds against a fixed amount of plant so there will be less secured," said Moody's analyst Emily Eisenlohr. "There are cash flow benefits to this transaction but that is one additional consideration that we are looking at."
Moody's review for upgrade is remains intact, she added.

Both high-grade and junk bond buyers are expected to dip in for the Ba2/BB rated deal, which is managed via Morgan Stanley & Co. Price talk is 90 basis points over Treasuries for five-year debt, 115 basis points over for seven-year debt, and 60 basis points over for insured 10-year debt.

Elsewhere, ABN AMRO Chicago's $750 million 10-year global subordinated debt offering was formally priced on Wednesday to yield 59 basis points over the curve, according to lead managers ABN AMRO and Goldman Sachs.

Other bank and finance sector offerings of Wednesday are $500 million in five-year debt from Associates Corp to be priced in Europe via Lehman Brothers and Morgan Stanley, and $500 million multi-tranche debt from Mercantile Bancorp via Salomon Brothers.
On Wednesday or Thursday, offerings also include $300 million five-year debt from Tenneco Inc via Credit Suisse First Boston and $650 million debt from Hartford Life.

"There is a lot of supply around and that's putting some pressure on the market, but there seems to be enough demand," said one syndicate chief at a midwestern investment bank. "We saw spread widening but the market is holding together well given all (the supply) that's coming."
Combined supply of high-grades, junk bonds and asset-backed securities is rapidly approaching the $20 billion mark for the week, the chief said.

In high-yields, issues set for pricing on Wednesday include $125 million 10-year Ba3/B-plus senior unsecured notes from Cott Corp via Morgan Stanley; $175 million 10-year senior secured notes from Pioneer Americas Acquisition Corp via Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette; and, possibly, $300 million two-part offering from Stage Stores' Specialty Retailers.

Mexican railroad transportation service provider TFM S.A. de C.V. on Wednesday may price $150 million in 10-year senior notes and $250 million in proceeds of zero coupon bonds through a Morgan Stanley group.

Later this week, Chase Telecommunications Inc will issue $125 million in zero coupon bonds through a Credit Suisse First Boston syndicate. The offering is expected to price with a yield near 14 percent and warrants for 15 to 17 percent of the company, said a source close to the deal.
It is the first zero coupon from a start-up telecom company in several months.
